Hi Sofie — thanks for the heads up and the screenshot.

Quick notes:
- Calendly should respect your browser/Google timezone, but some corporate G-Suite defaults can force a different zone when the ICS is injected.
- We have seen Chili Piper + Calendly duplicates when both systems surface an .ics and the recipient's calendar auto-accepts both.

I'll send a manual .ics in Europe/Stockholm (CEST) to lock the 10:00–10:45 slot. Looping in Marissa (our SDR) and Neha (who handles scheduler integrations) to make sure we avoid duplicate invites.

Apologies for the friction — I’ll attach an explicit ICS and a short note to ACME's IT so they can prevent auto-accept for duplicates.

— Karthik

Karthik / Neha — quick tech note from ops:
- If the landing page has both a Chili Piper widget and a Calendly link (we've done this during AB tests) some browsers prefetch and both services issue provisional invites. That causes duplicate ICS files to be generated.
- The safest workaround: (1) disable automatic ICS generation on the page for the active widget, (2) send a manual ICS from our calendar (explicit TZ), and (3) paste a one-line instruction in the invite: "If you receive a duplicate invite, please delete the one labeled 'ChiliPiper' or with a different timezone."

I can push the landing page update (30–60 mins) but for speed let's send the manual invite and copy ACME IT. I'll also include a short bullet they can paste into their calendar auto-accept rules.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
SDR Lead | Redwood Inference
